question_text: The Nation's first motto was 'E Pluribus Unum.' What does that mean?

why_it_matters.text: 'E Pluribus Unum' is Latin for 'Out of many, one.' Originally it meant 13 separate colonies becoming one nation. Today it means something even bigger: people from many countries, languages, religions, and backgrounds becoming one American people. It still appears on most U.S. coins and the Great Seal of the United States — the official symbol of our country.

fun_fact.text: On July 4, 1776 — the same day Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence — they chose Benjamin Franklin, John Adams, and Thomas Jefferson to design a national seal. The trio proposed 'E Pluribus Unum.' Look closely: the phrase has exactly 13 letters — one for each original colony.
